newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen quiet in Xmas week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen quiet in Xmas week.

text.p: Christmas dominates the week and is expected to keep financial markets quiet.
The one piece of Statistics Bureau data to be released, new motor vehicle registrations for November, are hardly expected to cause a stir.
The combination of their Christmas Eve release and the recent volatility in the monthly data means that the series will in all probability be igonored by the market, economists said.
The Australian dollar is expected to ignore the registrations data, and the market is expected to be pretty thin.

The stronger finish to the past week of the Australian dollar may bias the tone to the upside, but with dealing rooms on skeleon staff and most books already closed off for the year, traders said the direction of the dollar will be dictated by offshore trends.
Stocks are seen firmer this week with buyers on Friday showing no signs of quitting, providing Wall Street keeps showing the way.
Wall Street climbed further on Friday, with the Dow rising 10.76 to close at 6484.4 after a volatile day.
Local features are thin on the ground with corporate activity virtually nil in the Christmas week.
The only sign of life may come from Advance Bank shareholders who meet on Monday to vote on the merger proposal with St George Bank.
Otherwise, all eyes remain on a seemingly resurgent Wall Street with few local leads seen or expected.

Australian bonds are expected to start the week guided by U.S. Treasuries which ended lower after profit-taking dragged prices off early peaks and disappointment with a nuance of Federal Reserve policy prompted late selling in thin trade but turnover will stay thin ahead of the Christmas break.
With only November motor registrations due out on Christmas Eve, the local market is expected to stay very much in tandem with the U.S. market.
SFE floor trading will finish at 1.10 p.m. on Tuesday and will resume the following Tuesday. There will be no overnight SYCOM trade on Tuesday.
SYCOM trade will be available from 8.30 a.m. to 4.30 p.m. on Friday and from 6.30 p.m. on Friday to 7.00 a.m. on Saturday.
